title: The lost Blues Alley job in Washington and a New Orleans engagement
summary: A promised Washington club job falls through when the owner sells, while a New Orleans band job briefly pays $1,500 a week.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: And, by the time you moved to Washington, when you were still scraping along too, you still were doing all right - I mean -you had managed to collect a bunch of good furniture.
Oh - yeah and all of that.

Oh, sure - but I'm saying, we were not in a position to save anything-- any money. We were just-- we were making it, and living well but not saving any money and I don't think anyone is doing good if you can't save some of the money you make. And, so, we came up here and we had a very bad disappointment up here--
Yeah -- we had a promise of The Blues Alley job, which never came off; the guy changed his mind in the middle of the road--
Did he change his mind or did he sell out?

Well, sold it on top of that - yes - but he should have told me that before he got me up here and all that. So, these are the kind of things that happen -- from time to time. We went down to New Orleans on a job -- I took a band down there for awhile and made myself $1,500.00 a week and the band making almost $1,000.00 each on this job with our hotel and everything; you almost think you're back in business again, but after that, then
you're back in the same old fight again.
